etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French escouade, from Italian squadra (“square”) (whence also French escadre). Doublet of squadra and square.

definitions.definition: A unit of tactical military personnel, or of police officers, usually of about ten members.

quote.text: A squad of soldiers ordered them to disperse but instead of doing so they commenced throwing ice and rocks.

definitions.definition: (cricket, soccer, rugby) A group of potential players from whom a starting team and substitutes are chosen.
(informal) A collective noun for a group of squid.

quote.text: At one point, the 400-ton Calypso was brought to a standstill by a squad of squid which clogged the engines and caused a power failure. Other, highlights included an attack by predatory blue sharks,  […]

quote.citation: 2002, Let's Go Inc., Let's Go 2003: Britain & Ireland, Let's Go Publications:
quote.text: The Sea Life Centre retains a squad of squid and such.

quote.citation: 2012, S. Louis King, Gnome Home Papers, AuthorHouse, →ISBN, page 546:
quote.text: There's several new symbols next to the doorway symbol. Beso pushed all six of them without waiting to see what they brought; like a herd of charging rhinos or rampaging squad of squid. Next best thing though.

quote.citation: 2017, Kristen Joy Wilks, Athens Ambuscade, Pelican Ventures Book Group, →ISBN:
quote.text: I  pulled in as deep a breath as my gag allowed and began relaxing my body. I used a little trick I'd learned in college. I imagined that a friendly squad of squid were massaging every muscle on the bottoms of my feet; the tension began to drain.

definitions.definition: A group of people organized for some common purpose, usually of about ten members.
(slang) One's friend group, taken collectively; one's peeps.

quote.citation: 2019, Bernardine Evaristo, Girl, Woman, Other, Penguin Books (2020), page 52:
quote.text: anyway, sheʼs resigned herself to hanging out with the squad at uni rather than going manhunting

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To act as part of, or on behalf of, a squad.
(transitive, US, medical slang) To transport by ambulance.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: Uncertain. Compare squick (“disgust”), squalid (“dirty”) with similar initial sounds.

quote.citation: 1875 March 13, Leicester Chronicle, quoted in the EDD:
quote.text: The lass ran all among the muck and squad.

quote.citation: 1895, Alfred Tennyson, The Poetical Works of Alfred Tennyson: Poet-laureate, page 791:
quote.text: An' she did n't not solidly mean I wur / gawin' that waäy to the bad,Fur the gell was as howry a trollope as / iver traäpes'd i' the squad.
